$comment: Accepted-problem baseline for scripts/check-railway-deploy-drift.mjs.
The drift check fails on any service that is not running the head commit and is
NOT listed here. An entry means: this service is known to be behind a refused push,
it has an owner issue, and it must not page again until that issue moves.
Entries are matched on service:verdict exactly, and the split is the same one
scripts/check-seed-freshness.mjs applies to compact health -- same function, so
expiry and prune-on-recovery cannot drift into two different meanings.
A service that recovers is reported as 'recovered' on the next run (prune it).
A service that fails with a DIFFERENT verdict than the one baselined blocks,
which is the point: BEHIND on a service baselined for REJECTED_PUSH is a new
failure wearing an old name -- the filter was cleared and it went stale anyway.
The 62 REJECTED_PUSH entries are the measured fleet as of 2026-08-04: every
service carrying a Railway watch-path filter was running code older than a push
Railway had refused (#6141). They are acknowledged rather than fixed because
clearing the filters costs ~2250 build-minutes/day and restarts four always-on
services on every merge; #6142 replaces the mechanism instead. This list should
SHRINK as #6142 lands, and every entry it removes is one the check will tell you
to prune.
expiresAt forces a re-review of the whole file. A stale-deploy suppression that
outlives its cause is how a fleet ends up silently a week behind.

acknowledged.name: umami
acknowledged.reason: The analytics collector stopped receiving deployments from the GitHub integration on 2026-08-03. Its watch paths are already empty, so this is the webhook-side sibling of #6141 rather than a filter rejection -- and the failure that proves this check must not key on the filter: no SKIPPED record exists, and the service is a day behind head.

acknowledged.name: ais-relay
acknowledged.reason: Carries a Railway watch-path filter, which refused a push and has built nothing since. Railway builds the full tree at a SHA, so the change rides the next build that fires — this is lag (p90 19h, max 62.6h fleet-wide), not loss. Measured 2026-08-04; the filter stays until #6142 shortens the tail by triggering deploys from CI.
